Can you confirm Redwood can accept the addition of those subprocessors and whether Redwood prefers DocuSign or AdobeSign for the execution? HorizonCare wants a one-envelope flow with countersignature.

Subject: Re: DPA supplement for 2027 renewal - new subprocessors

Hi Roberta — thanks for the heads up.

Quick answers up front:
- Redwood can generally accept CloudCache (logging/cache provider) and DataShard (analytics subprocessor) pending a standard security questionnaire/attestation from each vendor.
- We use AdobeSign for enterprise customer execution by default, but we can accommodate DocuSign if HorizonCare requires it.

I'll loop Legal for final confirmation on the language (we prefer an addendum that references the existing DPA and includes a signer-rotation block so future minor subprocessor swaps do not require full reexecution). Vivek, Marissa — can you weigh in on the suggested addendum wording and whether we should include EU transfer language (SCCs) in this supplement?

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Director, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-05T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA supplement - proposed language attached

Evelyn — drafting note attached.

Summary of proposed changes (high level):
- New Exhibit A-1 listing CloudCache and DataShard with description of processing and subprocess transmissions.
- Clause: "Limited Consent for Subprocessor Replacement" — allows Redwood to swap equivalent subprocessors with 15 days' notice unless HorizonCare objects with reasonable cause.
- Data transfer paragraph referencing SCCs for EU-origin data and committing to customer notice + option for dedicated region.

I attached a redline (HorizonCare_DPA_Supplement_v1.1.pdf). Karthik assigned a short vendor attestation questionnaire to CloudCache/DataShard and will follow up.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA supplement - vendor attestations

Quick update: we reached out to both CloudCache and DataShard. Expected turn-around for the security attest is ~7 business days. No red flags in the first pass.

One ask from Legal / InfoSec: add a short sentence in Exhibit A-1 that any processing of EU personal data will be subject to SCCs unless we are operating in a pinned EU region. Not negotiation heavy but prevents confusion down the line.

Karthik
